articles.title: EU countries block Canada's 'associate membership' plan
articles.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wanted to give Canada a special status within the EU. But Germany and other member states have raised objections ahead of a summit in Montreal.

image.caption: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen are seeking closer ties between Canada and the EU [FILE: September 16, 2026]Image: Justin Tang/The Canadian Press/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: European Union member states have blocked a proposal by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to grant Canada a special status as an "associate member" of the bloc.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and several other EU leaders pushed to remove the term from a draft declaration ahead of a two-day EU-Canada summit beginning Thursday in Montreal, according to diplomats cited by the dpa and AFP news agencies.
Instead, the revised document calls for a plan to establish "closer ties" between Canada and the EU without membership.

blocks.caption: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met German Chancellor Friedrich Merz at the Chancellery in Berlin in August 2025 [FILE: August 26, 2025]Image: Annegret Hilse/REUTERS

blocks.text: The declaration was approved by EU member states on Wednesday evening and is expected to be published on Friday, at the end of the summit.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, von der Leyen, European Council President Antonio Costa and several EU commissioners are attending the talks.
Why did EU countries oppose Canada's associate membership?
Von der Leyen first proposed making Canada the EU's first "associate member" in September during a speech attended by Carney.
Canada's PM welcomes EU associate membership idea
However, the proposal raised questions among member states because existing EU treaties do not provide for such a status.
Diplomats said several governments were concerned about the lack of clarity surrounding the proposed arrangement and insufficient consultation between the European Commission and EU member states.
Germany, France and Italy were among the countries that raised objections, although they broadly support closer cooperation with Canada.
Another concern was that the term "associate membership" had already been used in discussions about Ukraine's potential accession to the EU.

Merz had previously suggested such a status for Ukraine as an intermediate step toward full membership. Under his proposal, Kyiv could participate in EU summits and ministerial meetings without voting rights.
Von der Leyen, however, used the same term to describe a different arrangement for Canada, a country that does not have a legal path to EU membership.

blocks.caption: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed making Canada an "associate member" of the EU during a speech at the European Parliament in Strasbourg in September [FILE: September 16, 2026]Image: Yves Herman/REUTERS

blocks.text: An earlier draft of the summit declaration would have allowed Canada to participate in consultations on major EU political and regulatory initiatives as an associate member.
It also called for the full scope of the arrangement to be defined by the 2027 EU-Canada summit.
Carney, meanwhile, played down the dispute over the wording of the summit declaration.
He said the precise terminology mattered less than the practical benefits closer cooperation would bring to Canadians.
What will closer EU-Canada cooperation involve?
Despite the disagreement over terminology, both sides intend to significantly deepen their partnership.
The revised declaration focuses on an "Alliance for the Future," a term Carney has frequently used to describe relations between Canada and the EU.
The initiative aims to remove trade barriers, facilitate investment and secure supplies of critical raw materials, medicines and technologies during crises.
As Trump menaces, some think Canada should join the EU
Both sides also want to strengthen cooperation on energy, climate protection, artificial intelligence, security and education.
Canada could gain broader access to EU programs covering research, education and defense.
A new economic council is planned to bring together businesses from both sides of the Atlantic.
The declaration also calls for a study into the feasibility of increasing Canadian liquefied natural gas exports to Europe.
However, EU governments watered down several economic commitments in the original draft.

An explicit goal of deeper financial market integration was removed. Instead of promising preferential treatment in economic security measures, both sides now intend to limit potential negative effects on each other.
How has Donald Trump affected EU-Canada relations?
The push for closer ties comes amid growing uncertainty over relations with the United States under President Donald Trump.
Trade disputes, US tariffs and Trump's territorial claims have raised concerns in both Canada and Europe about Washington's reliability as a partner.
Both sides hope that closer cooperation will help reduce their dependence on other countries and strengthen their ability to pursue common interests.
How could Trump react to Canada-EU association plan?
Trump previously dismissed the idea of Canadian associate membership in the EU as ridiculous.
He also threatened consequences if the arrangement harmed US interests, warning that he could impose high tariffs or halt trade with Europe in several sectors.

articles.title: What’s at stake for Trump in Israel’s deadlocked election?
articles.summary: The outcome will have implications for US-Israeli relations, which have been dominated by the joint fight against Iran, stalled Gaza peace efforts and signs of eroding US public support for Israel

blocks.text: TRUMP AND NETANYAHU. US President Donald Trump welcomes Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the entrance of the White House in Washington, DC, USA, April 7, 2025.
Leah Millis/Reuters
The outcome will have implications for US-Israeli relations, which have been dominated by the joint fight against Iran, stalled Gaza peace efforts and signs of eroding US public support for Israel

items: Israel's recent election resulted in no clear winner, leading to uncertainty for President Trump regarding US-Israeli relations amid ongoing challenges from Iran and Gaza.

Prime Minister Netanyahu's bloc secured the most seats but lacks a parliamentary majority, setting the stage for potential coalition negotiations or another election while he remains in a caretaker role.
The election outcome may impact Trump's strategy against Iran and hinder progress on Gaza peace efforts, as both potential leaders maintain tough stances on security and negotiations.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

WASHINGTON, USA – With Israel’s election yielding no clear winner, President Donald Trump could face prolonged uncertainty over who will lead Washington’s closest Middle East ally as he confronts challenges from Iran and Gaza across the region.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc secured the most seats in Israel’s parliament but still lost its parliamentary majority on Tuesday, October 27, despite Trump having endorsed him against a rival alliance of parties led by hawkish former military chief Gadi Eisenkot.

While Netanyahu seemed in a stronger position, neither side was projected to have an outright path to form a new government after Israel’s first election since the Hamas-led attacks of October 7, 2023, and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

blocks.caption: Netanyahu set to remain caretaker after inconclusive Israeli election

blocks.text: The stage appeared to be set for a period of painstaking coalition bargaining – or possibly another election – while Netanyahu remains in power in a caretaker capacity.
The outcome will have implications for US-Israeli relations, which have been dominated by the joint fight against Iran, stalled Gaza peace efforts and signs of eroding US public support for Israel.
The uncertainty comes at a sensitive moment for Trump, when he and Netanyahu have threatened to join in another round of attacks against Iran.

“Israeli politics can be messy,” said Aaron David Miller, a former Middle East adviser in Democratic and Republican administrations. From the US perspective, he said, “it would be good to get some clarity, but that’s easier said than done.”

Netanyahu – a consummate political survivor who has had a close but sometimes turbulent relationship with Trump dating back decades – may have survived again. He is the longest-serving Israeli prime minister and the only one the US president has ever worked with.

Eisenkot, who projected an image as a ⁠political outsider and security-minded former general during the campaign, has seen his governing chances dimmed but not extinguished. He is not known to have ever met Trump.

Some analysts say creation of a broad unity government keeping Netanyahu in power might serve Trump’s interest in a politically stable Israeli partner. But neither side has shown a willingness to take that path.
Asked whether he was going to get involved in an effort to form a Netanyahu-led unity government, Trump told Axios on Wednesday he hadn’t thought about it, adding: “I will take a look.”

Topping the list is how Trump might engage with Israel in the war against Iran, which has rocked the Middle East. The eight-month-old conflict has disrupted global energy supplies, pushed up US gasoline prices and driven down his approval ratings, imperiling his Republicans’ control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections.

Trump, in his October 18 endorsement, insisted he wanted Netanyahu to remain in power to help him soon “finish the job” against Iran. The president said overnight that Netanyahu, who outperformed pre-election polls, had done “very well” and that his backing had boosted the Israeli leader.

Trump has repeatedly signaled that the US and Israel could restart attacks on Iran after the midterms, with some critics, including in Israel, suggesting Netanyahu might see it as a way to bolster his political standing as caretaker prime minister.

Jonathan Panikoff, a former deputy US national intelligence officer on the Middle East, said any future Israeli leadership would likely be on the same page as Trump if he decides to escalate from the current stalemate with Israel’s regional arch-foe.
“It’s hard to imagine any real daylight between them on that point,” said Panikoff, now at the Atlantic Council think tank in Washington.
Where Netanyahu and many Israelis have sometimes differed with Trump is when he has offered concessions in now-stalled negotiations with the Islamic Republic.
No matter how Israel’s next government shapes up, there is little reason to believe there will be any sweeping shift in tough policies toward the Palestinians.

This doesn’t bode well for breaking the diplomatic deadlock between Israel and Hamas and fully implementing Trump’s Gaza peace plan following the war there. Israel, in response to the militants’ deadly cross-border attack, leveled much of the enclave and killed tens of thousands of Palestinians.
Administration officials have privately expressed frustration over what they see as intransigence by Netanyahu, who has insisted that Hamas must first disarm.

Eisenkot, who lost a son and two nephews in the Gaza war, stressed his military credentials while positioning himself as a centrist domestically during the election campaign. He has vowed to break with Netanyahu’s far-right coalition allies, but not with the hawkish approach to security that has become more entrenched since the 2023 Hamas attack. – Rappler.com

With nearly 86% of votes tallied on Wednesday, Israel’s three main broadcasters projected Netanyahu’s bloc of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties would win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, well ahead of the 48 for rival Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc.

Parties representing Arab Israelis were projected to win an unprecedented 19 seats, leaving Eisenkot little realistic path to power without their broad backing, which many Jewish political leaders reject.

blocks.caption: Israeli exit polls show deadlock, setback for Netanyahu

blocks.text: The results could still change as counting continued, but Eisenkot’s bloc of anti-Netanyahu parties, ranging from the center-left to the hard right, had fallen short of pre-election polls that forecast a tight race.

Netanyahu would remain caretaker prime minister during any coalition negotiations and potentially until another election next year. While a caretaker government faces some constraints, experts say it retains powers, including over the war with Iran.

Guy Lurie, a research fellow at the Israel Democracy Institute, said a caretaker government formally had the same powers as a regular government, but also “a duty of restraint” and less discretion in some areas.
Netanyahu, addressing his Likud party’s faithful after 3 am (0100 GMT), called for the formation of “a strong, right-wing national government.”

He highlighted Israel’s military successes and raised the prospect of renewed joint military action against Iran alongside his ally, US President Donald Trump, saying the two countries had a “singular historical opportunity” to remove what he called the Iranian threat “once and for all.”

Trump, who had urged Israeli voters to keep Netanyahu in power so the two leaders could “finish the job” in Iran, said Netanyahu had done “very well” and claimed his endorsement had “helped him a lot.”
Israel’s high-turnout vote was brushed aside by some in the rest of the Middle East.

In Tehran, banners with images of slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei reminded Iranians of US and Israeli strikes launched in February which kicked off the war. Just to the right was a poster of late Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah, who was killed on Netanyahu’s orders in Lebanon.
“I genuinely see the possibility of attack,” said 50-year-old Iranian citizen Abdollah Karimi.
Frustration was also palpable in Egypt, the first Arab country to make peace with Israel in 1979.
Outhman Selim, a 62-year-old lawyer, said his hopes that a Netanyahu defeat would steer the country away from the far right had been dashed.
Eisenkot acknowledged that Netanyahu remained caretaker prime minister but warned that he might use security for political ends.

“I call on the heads of the security establishment and the civil service: Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate or the people’s trust,” he said. “Stand firm in the face of any attempt to challenge you.”
Netanyahu’s office has previously rejected accusations that he is using the Iran conflict for political gain and did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Wednesday.

The prospect of a caretaker government without a parliamentary majority weighed on Israeli markets. The shekel ILS= currency weakened around 1.6% to 3.10 to the US dollar. Tel Aviv’s key benchmark stock indexes fell more than 3%.

The result underscored the rightward shift among Israeli Jews during Netanyahu’s years as the country’s dominant political figure. The center-left that dominated Israel for the first half of its history has been reduced to a small fringe.
Nearly all Jewish parties now share Netanyahu’s rejection of an eventual independent Palestinian state, the basis of internationally endorsed peace efforts since the 1990s.
The election was Israel’s first since Hamas-led fighters killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostages in attacks on October 7, 2023, that plunged the country into wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.
The war in Gaza, which flattened the territory and killed 74,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza health authorities, has left Israel increasingly isolated on the world stage.
Netanyahu himself is wanted by the International Criminal Court in The Hague on war crimes charges he calls absurd, and faces corruption charges in Israel that he dismisses as an establishment plot.

Turnout reached 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades, and was particularly high among Israelis of Palestinian descent, who make up more than a fifth of the population. Many were motivated by what they see as open racism from Netanyahu’s cabinet, which includes a party leader convicted of inciting racial hatred against Arabs.

The headquarters of the Joint List, an alliance of several Arab parties, burst into whistles and applause when exit polls were released. “We refuse the occupation and racism, and we will remain here,” said Joint List candidate Faten Gattas.

The coalition that last toppled Netanyahu relied on one small Arab party, but Eisenkot’s underperformance means the opposition would now need backing from the Joint List itself. Most Jewish leaders have shunned formal alliances with Arab parties since Israel’s founding. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 8:03am

United States Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Wednesday announced an increase in the US Department of War's security cooperation funds to accelerate the modernization of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP).

“Secretary Hegseth announced an increase in the Department of War's security cooperation funds to accelerate the AFP's modernization and enhance interoperability along the First Island Chain,” a readout released by the US Department of War stated.
However, the US Department of War did not specify the amount of the increase in security cooperation funds.
The announcement was made during Hegseth's meeting with Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr.

The two defense officials discussed progress in security cooperation, alliance modernization, and posture initiatives as the Philippines and the United States continued efforts to strengthen their defense partnership.
Hegseth and Teodoro also agreed to launch an alliance command and control modernization sprint to improve real-time bilateral coordination and strengthen the resilience of the alliance.

They also welcomed progress in operationalizing sites under the bilateral Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA), including investments in critical infrastructure and storage facilities across the Philippines.
The Philippines is hosting the 20th ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) and the 13th ADMM-Plus on October 28 and 29 in Cebu.
ADMM is ASEAN's highest defense consultative and cooperative mechanism, according to the Department of National Defense (DND).
The ADMM-Plus expands defense cooperation to eight dialogue partners including Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia, and the United States. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: [Ask the Tax Whiz] BIR e-invoicing: Is your company ready for December 31?
articles.summary: This affects billing, customer records, accounting systems, and the controls that keep transactions accurate and traceable

blocks.text: The Philippine Tax Whiz explains what Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 98-2026 means for large taxpayers, multinational companies, and digital businesses—from permits and system requirements to branch coverage and billing errors.

Your company may already issue thousands of invoices through a global accounting system. But can it generate structured invoice data, deliver invoices electronically, and meet Philippine authorization requirements?
Under Revenue Memorandum Circular (RMC) No. 98-2026, covered taxpayers must comply with electronic invoicing requirements on or before December 31, 2026.

For chief financial officers, tax directors, and technology teams, this is a business readiness issue. It affects billing, customer records, accounting systems, and the controls that keep transactions accurate and traceable.
The circular identifies the following covered taxpayers, subject to its exemption for micro taxpayers:

items: Small, medium, and large taxpayers engaged in e-commerce or internet transactions;
Taxpayers under the jurisdiction of the Large Taxpayers Service (LTS);
Taxpayers classified as large under the Ease of Paying Taxes Act and Revenue Regulation (RR) No. 8-2024;
Taxpayers using a Computerized Accounting System (CAS), Computerized Books of Accounts with Accounting Records with electronic invoicing, or other invoicing software; and
Other taxpayers required by the Commissioner of Internal Revenue.

blocks.text: Companies should assess each applicable category. Being outside the Large Taxpayers Service (LTS) does not, by itself, establish exemption.
The definition of e-commerce also extends beyond online retail. It includes commercial transactions involving physical or digital goods and services conducted through electronic networks.

A Philippine subsidiary or registered branch should assess its own taxpayer classification, activities, and invoicing systems. Foreign ownership or the use of a regional billing center does not replace that assessment.
For multinational groups, the practical questions are: Which entity makes the sale? Which entity issues the invoice? Does its system meet Philippine requirements?

Nonresident digital service providers require a separate analysis. RR No. 3-2025 contains specific invoicing rules for nonresident VAT-registered providers, allowing electronic sales or commercial invoices that need not be registered with the BIR, provided prescribed information and language requirements are met. Companies should therefore avoid assuming that the domestic Permit to Issue (PTI) process automatically applies to every overseas platform selling to Philippine customers. (READ: [Ask the Tax Whiz] Guidelines on VAT for Nonresident Digital Service Providers)
An emailed PDF alone does not establish compliance.
Under RMC No. 98-2026, an electronic invoice must:

items: Be generated through duly registered, approved, or accredited accounting or invoicing software in a structured electronic format;
Be electronically generated and delivered through recognized electronic channels, such as email, online viewing, QR codes, applications, or web platforms; and
Contain data capable of electronic extraction, processing, and transmission to the BIR for sales reporting.

blocks.text: Invoices manually prepared using Word, Excel, Google Docs, Google Sheets, or similar productivity applications do not qualify.
A PDF may serve as the customer-facing copy of a compliant system-generated invoice. The underlying structured data and system capabilities remain essential.
Printed copies are also allowed under the circular and must be provided upon the buyer’s request. Printing an invoice does not cure a system that lacks the required electronic capabilities.
The circular separates electronic invoice issuance from electronic sales reporting.
Electronic invoicing concerns generating and issuing compliant invoices. Electronic sales reporting concerns transmitting sales data to the BIR.

Under RMC No. 98-2026, the electronic sales reporting obligation for the covered taxpayers is subject to the BIR’s issuance of implementing policies, guidelines, and procedures. The requirement to secure a Permit to Transmit applies upon notification or directive from the Commissioner.
Companies must prepare systems capable of transmission, but should not confuse that technical capability with an across-the-board reporting commencement date.
Taxpayers must secure a Permit to Issue (PTI) Electronic Invoice before generating or issuing electronic invoices.

The application must be filed with the Revenue District Office or Large Taxpayer Office where the taxpayer is registered, supported by the prescribed documents. The circular provides for evaluation and determination of compliance within 20 working days from receipt of complete documents.
An existing CAS Permit to Use or Acknowledgement Certificate does not, by itself, authorize electronic invoice issuance.
Taxpayers must also obtain Electronic Invoicing and Sales Reporting (EIS) Certification within six months from PTI issuance. Failure to obtain certification constitutes grounds for PTI revocation.

The certification validates the system’s ability to extract, process, and transmit sales data according to BIR standards. Technical specifications and guides are available through the EIS Certification Portal⁠.
The six-month certification period should not be treated as an extension of the December 31 invoicing deadline.
The circular allows an in-house solution, commercially acquired software, or services offered by an Electronic Invoicing Service Provider (ESP).

It also permits businesses to retain other structured formats for internal operations, provided the required sales data can be converted into and transmitted using the BIR-prescribed format. The existing EIS uses JavaScript Object Notation, or JSON, for sales data transmission.
For multinationals, this means assessing whether the current enterprise resource planning system can support Philippine requirements through configuration or integration.

As a practical readiness exercise, finance and IT teams should test customer and taxpayer identifiers, branch information, VAT treatment, discounts, withholding tax details, invoice references, and reconciliation with accounting records.

The circular reserves ESP policies and guidelines for a separate issuance. Businesses should verify a provider’s claimed authorization and distinguish vendor marketing from the taxpayer’s own permit and certification requirements.
Yes. Where the taxpayer is covered, compliance extends to its head office and all registered branches, even if the covered activity takes place only at a particular branch.

The circular provides for PTIs for the head office and individual branches bearing the same PTI number and identifying the relevant branch. However, each distinct invoicing system requires a separate PTI, identifying the offices or locations authorized to use it.
Changes to the approved platform or core system details—including migration or replacement—require a new or amended PTI, as applicable.
For corporations with multiple billing platforms, mapping systems to branches and business units should therefore be an early implementation step.
The obligation to issue invoices continues.

Where an interruption prevents electronic invoice issuance, the taxpayer must issue a BIR-authorized manual invoice. Once the system is restored, the manual invoices must be replaced with corresponding electronic invoices bearing their reference numbers.

For businesses, this calls for a documented contingency procedure: authorized manual invoices, clear staff responsibilities, and reconciliation after restoration to prevent missed or duplicate recording of sales.
No. Issued electronic invoices cannot be deleted, altered, or modified.
Corrections must use a separate document referencing the original invoice:

items: A decrease in the amount requires a duly authorized credit note or credit memo.
An increase requires a new electronic invoice.

blocks.text: If an invoice incorrectly states ₱50,000 instead of ₱5,000, a ₱45,000 credit note or memo corrects the overstatement while preserving the original record.

Companies should review whether their billing systems permit users to overwrite issued invoices. Approval controls and traceable adjustments are particularly important for high-volume billing, refunds, and subscription changes.
Moving to a lower classification does not automatically end the obligation. A covered taxpayer must continue complying unless the BIR expressly provides otherwise through a separate issuance.

For upward reclassification, the circular refers to a compliance period prescribed by the BIR that must not be less than six months from reclassification. This should not be described as a universal requirement to comply “within six months.”

Assign a joint finance, tax, and IT team to confirm coverage, map invoicing systems and branches, identify required changes, prepare PTI applications, and schedule certification testing. Include invoice corrections and outage recovery in testing—not just successful invoice generation.

Electronic invoicing can improve transaction visibility, reduce manual reconciliation, and strengthen tax administration. But implementation must also deliver clearer rules, secure systems, and less repetitive compliance.

For companies navigating complex systems or uncertain requirements, investing in advice from qualified tax experts early can help identify compliance gaps, prevent costly mistakes, and avoid unnecessary penalties and stress.

Electronic invoicing should make honest compliance easier—and deliberate tax evasion harder. Its success should translate into better data, simpler processes, and a more predictable environment for business and investment. – Rappler.com
For more tax information and inquiries, visit www.acg.ph⁠.

Mon Abrea, CPA, MBA, MPA (Harvard) is a global tax policy expert and Chief Tax Advisor of Asian Consulting Group (ACGlobal). He advises governments, multinational enterprises, and international organizations on tax policy, investment competitiveness, and fiscal reform. He is the author of Reimagining the World Without Corruption and Why Invest in the Philippines? CREATE MORE Edition, and has represented the Philippines in policy dialogues at the OECD, World Bank, and other international forums.

articles.title: PH, Japan eye transfer of first Abukuma-class destroyer 'at the earliest possible date'
articles.summary: PH, Japan eye transfer of first Abukuma-class destroyer 'at the earliest possible date"

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 7:38am
The Philippines and Japan are working on transfer of the first Abukuma-class destroyer to the Philippine Navy at the earliest possible date.
In a joint statement after a defense meeting on Wednesday, the two countries said the Japanese warship will be transferred following its expected decommissioning in the coming years.

“Through this transfer, the two Ministers confirmed their intention to deepen comprehensive cooperation encompassing vessel operations, logistics support, human resource development, and information sharing, thereby taking defense cooperation, particularly in the field of maritime security, to a new level,” the joint statement read.

“They further confirmed that such cooperation would make a significant contribution to collaboration with allies and like-minded countries, thereby helping to ensuring peace and stability in the region,” it added.

Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. and Japanese Defense Minister Koizumi Shinjiro said defense authorities from both countries had agreed to pursue the transfer following discussions within a working group established in May.
Based on a report from Japanese media in July 2025, Tokyo is set to export six warships to the Philippines.
Teodoro and Koizumi also agreed to provide the necessary education and training for Philippine Navy personnel before the transfer and to cooperate closely on the vessel's maintenance and sustainment.

The planned transfer is expected to deepen Philippines-Japan defense cooperation, particularly in maritime security, through collaboration in vessel operations, logistics support, human resource development, and information sharing.
Teodoro and Koizumi said the cooperation would also contribute to collaboration with allies and like-minded countries, helping promote peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region.

The announcement came as the Philippines and Japan reaffirmed their opposition to unilateral attempts to change the status quo by force or coercion in the East China Sea and the South China Sea (SCS).

They also expressed serious concerns over China's increasingly frequent and extensive coercive activities in the waters and airspace surrounding Japan, as well as its dangerous and coercive actions against the Philippines in the South China Sea.
The two countries further committed to strengthening their bilateral defense ties under their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and advancing efforts toward a Free and Open Indo-Pacific.
Meanwhile, the defense officials also agreed to discuss operational and maintenance arrangements for the transfer of a TC-90 aircraft to the Philippines by the end of Japan's fiscal year 2027.
They also agreed to accelerate discussions on defense equipment and technology cooperation, including efforts to strengthen the production base for defense equipment.

The Philippines and Japan have expanded military cooperation through joint exercises and agreements, including the Reciprocal Access Agreement and the Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreement, which took effect in July 2026.
The Philippines is hosting the 20th ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) and the 13th ADMM-Plus on October 28 and 29 in Cebu.
ADMM is ASEAN's highest defense consultative and cooperative mechanism, according to the Department of National Defense (DND).
The ADMM-Plus expands defense cooperation to eight dialogue partners including Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia, and the United States. —VAL, GMA News

articles.summary: Apple has recently announced the new MacBook Pro PROLED XDR Display that comes with something many users have been wanting — a touch screen. Available in 14- and 16-inch models, the new MacBook…

blocks.text: Apple has recently announced the new MacBook Pro PROLED XDR Display that comes with something many users have been wanting — a touch screen.

blocks.caption: macbook touchscreen

blocks.text: Available in 14- and 16-inch models, the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display features up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness, 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, a 120Hz variable refresh rate, and a wider color gamut covering both P3 and Adobe RGB.
Touch screen for the first time

The new MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time. Users can scroll through a webpage with a swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. The touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.

blocks.caption: MacBook Pro Touch Screen

blocks.text: Fully decked out

Just for kicks we decked out the new touch screen MacBook Pro with the highest chipset, memory, storage, and apps. The total cost ramped up to more than 1 million pesos. We chose the M5 Max Chip with the 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU, a display with Nano-texture glass that bumps the cost up by almost P10,000, 128GB of unified memory. 16TB of storage, abd copies of both Final Cut Pro (P19,990) and Logic Pro (P12,990) preinstalled. There’s also the option for Apple Care protection plan to insure your P1M device.
Joking aside, the base model of the PROLED XDR Display MacBook Pro is roughly 1/5 of that cost starting at P203,990 with the Education plan.
Pricing and Availability

items: The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display will be available soon at apple.com/ph/ and Apple Authorized Resellers.

The 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display featuring M5 Pro starts at ₱214,990 and ₱203,990 with education savings; and the 16-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display featuring M5 Pro starts at ₱249,990 and ₱234,990 with education savings.

The 14-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display featuring M5 Max starts at ₱329,990 and ₱307,990 with education savings; and the 16-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display featuring M5 Max starts at ₱344,990 and ₱322,990 with education savings.

articles.title: Many K-9 dogs are now too old for duty. Can the PNP train new ones fast enough?
articles.summary: Only 347 out of the required number of 510 police service dogs remain active, with even more set to retire by the end of 2026

blocks.text: Members of the Philippine National Police–Explosive Ordnance Disposal and Canine (EOD/K9) Unit line up with their handlers at Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City on March 10, 2026. A total of 26 explosive detection dogs that served in the police force for around eight years are set to retire and will be available for adoption to qualified individuals. Interested adopters who can provide proper care and a suitable home for the retired service dogs may contact PMSgt Manny Molina at 0946-409-0044 for details on the screening and adoption process.
Rappler
Only 347 out of the required number of 510 police service dogs remain active, with even more set to retire by the end of 2026

items: The Philippine National Police's K-9 units are crucial for detecting bombs and hazardous materials, but there is a significant shortage of active service dogs.
Currently, only 347 out of the ideal 510 police service dog slots are filled, with some units, like protection and security patrol, having no dogs available.
The Commission on Audit warns that the ongoing shortage and delays in training new dogs could hinder the PNP's ability to perform its essential functions.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – If you’ve seen a police dog on duty lately, you’ve likely come across one of the few ones left in active service.

Dogs are the stars of the Philippine National Police’s Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) and Canine Group — using their sniffing superpowers to catch subtleties on the scene that their human counterparts may miss.

K-9 dogs are most commonly deployed to detect bombs and any chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear hazards. By the National Police Commission’s (NAPOLCOM) standards, there should be at least 310 dogs of this type.

There should also be at least 80 dogs assigned to sniff around for narcotics and illegal substances. Meanwhile, units like search-and-rescue, combat-tracking, and protection and security patrol should get 40 dogs each.
Clearly, these furry heroes play an important role in the safety of Filipinos, but as of late, there are no longer enough of them due to old age.
The Commission on Audit’s (COA) report on the PNP on Wednesday, October 28, found that only 347 of the ideal 510 police service dog slots remain filled across all five specializations.
Most alarming is the protection and security patrol unit, which no longer has any dogs at all to deploy.
It doesn’t stop there. COA stated that 19 more dogs are set to retire by the end of the year, with a whopping 285 more projected to hang up their gears for good come 2030.
While the PNP’s EOD and Canine Group has already gathered a new batch of 148 trainable dogs, they have yet to actually be prepared for service as the PNP has to adjust its testing parameters.

COA warned that the severe shortage of active police service dogs would affect the PNP unit’s ability to fulfill its mandated functions. But with delays in training new canine recruits, can the PNP fill all 510 slots in time? – Rappler.com

articles.title: MTRCB reminds bus operators to screen only age-appropriate content for Undas
articles.summary: The Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) has started inspecting transport terminals across Metro Manila ahead of the expected surge of travelers heading to the provinces for…

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 7:16am

The Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) has started inspecting transport terminals across Metro Manila ahead of the expected surge of travelers heading to the provinces for All Saints’ Day, reminding bus operators to screen only age-appropriate content.
The spot inspections aim to ensure that films and other video content shown on buses comply with regulations, particularly as families and children are expected to travel during the Undas holiday.
MTRCB chairperson and CEO Lala Sotto urged transport terminals and operators to cooperate with the agency to ensure that content shown during trips is suitable for younger passengers.

“Hinihikayat namin ang kooperasyon ng mga transport terminals at operators nang masiguro natin na angkop mapanood ng mga batang pasahero ang mga ipapalabas sa mga bus habang sila ay pauwi ng probinsya para sa Undas,” Sotto said.

Under MTRCB Memorandum Circular No. 03-2024, or the “Rules Governing the Public Exhibition of Motion Picture and/or Trailers in Common Carriers and Other Public Places,” public utility vehicles may screen only films and trailers classified as General Audience (G) or Parental Guidance (PG).
The rules cover jeepneys, buses, vans, rail transport, taxis, passenger ships, ferry boats and commercial airplanes.
A G rating means a film is suitable for viewers of all ages, while a PG rating means younger viewers should be supervised by a parent or guardian.
During the inspections, MTRCB personnel reminded drivers and operators to ensure that all content shown to passengers complies with the prescribed classifications.
The inspections will continue through October 29, 2026.

The inspection and information campaign covers transport hubs in Muntinlupa, Las Piñas, Pasay, Parañaque, Quezon City, Taguig, Manila, Caloocan and Valenzuela, as well as Bocaue, Bulacan.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: MAP: Power plants in the Visayas grid
articles.summary: One in three power plants in the Visayas is fueled by coal, based on the Department of Energy's list of existing power plants, as of July 2026

blocks.text: One in three power plants in the Visayas is fueled by coal, based on the Department of Energy's list of existing power plants, as of July 2026

items: The Visayas grid relies heavily on renewable energy, yet is projected to face multiple red alerts in 2027 due to rising energy demand and system failures.

Unplanned outages of coal power plants, particularly in Cebu, are causing frequent grid alerts, with calls for decentralized energy solutions and battery energy storage systems to mitigate future risks.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

CEBU, Philippines – More than 50% of the Visayas grid’s power generation mix comes from renewable energy sources and yet the region is expected to face multiple red alerts in 2027 primarily due to its rising energy demand and multiple system failures.

Energy Secretary Sharon Garin attributed the problem to a lack of planning and the failure of the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) to secure ancillary services procurement agreements (ASPAs) for 250 megawatts of power reserves.
The NGCP disclosed in a September situation report that more than 1,500 megawatts were unavailable due to forced plant outages and reduced operating capacities even with imports from Luzon.

Garin said that the power reserves are supposed to offset the lack of supply in some areas and keep plants operating at a stable capacity, instead of putting them under immense stress to constantly produce energy.
But where are these plant outages happening? The Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities (ICSC), citing the Daily Guardian, noted the shutdown of the following coal plants in the region:

items: Therma Visayas Inc. Unit 1 (TVI 1) – 150 MW: Offline for 125 days since May 3; expected to return by September 15
Therma Visayas Inc. Unit 2 (TVI 2) – 150 MW: Offline for 6 days since September 9, but previously offline for 161 days from March 24 to August 31; no indicative return date
Panay Energy Development Corp. Unit 3 (PEDC 3) – 150 MW: Offline for 16 days since August 29; previously targeted to return by October 3 but was pushed to end-of-October
Cebu Energy Development Corp. Unit 1 (CEDC 1) – 82 MW: Offline for 42 days from July 24 to September 3

blocks.text: “Unplanned and extended outages from coal power plants are the primary driver of these frequent grid alerts, particularly during peak demand hours when the system has the least room to absorb the loss of a large generating unit,” the ICSC said.

Based on the DOE’s list of existing power plants as of July 31, 2026, one in three power plants in the Visayas is fueled by coal, contributing around 1,267 megawatts of dependable energy capacity in the region.
The energy generation mix varies across the region’s five island sub-grids: Cebu, Bohol, Panay, Negros, and Leyte-Samar.

Cebu is where a majority of the energy from coal is coming from, and hosts the coal-fired power plants that have been on forced and unplanned outages in recent months. The Cebu island sub-grid consists of coal (82.03%), diesel (12.94%), solar (4.93%), and hydroelectric (0.1%) power plants.
During the Cebu Energy Summit on October 12, the NGCP said that Cebu carries the largest share of the Visayas grid’s manual load dropping allocation, which was at 42%.

Bohol’s energy mix is primarily run by its diesel power plants. The Bohol In-Island Diesel Power Plant, operated by the Mapalad Power Corporation (MPC), provides 60 MW in dependable capacity, while Salcon Power Corporation’s (SPC) Tagbilaran City-based diesel power plant and power barge provide 16 MW and 29 MW, respectively.

Two-thirds of Panay’s energy mix relies on coal. Three units of the Panay Energy Development Corporation’s (PEDC) circulating fluidized bed coal-fired thermal power plants contribute a total of 317.4 MW in dependable capacity, and Palm Concepcion Power Corporation’s (PCPC) coal-fired thermal power plant provides up to 135 MW in dependable capacity.
It’s only in the Leyte-Samar and Negros island sub-grids where renewable energy holds more than half of the energy generation allocations.
Negros receives around 433.3 MW in dependable capacity from its solar power plants, while the Leyte-Samar sub-grid’s geothermal plants alone generate 634 MW in dependable capacity.

The road ahead is still long for Visayas’ energy mix as the DOE expects to see new base load plants between 2028 to 2030. Garin said that the new plants would come from coal, nuclear, diesel, and geothermal energy sources.

Alberto Dalusung III, Energy Transition Advisor at ICSC, told Rappler in an interview on October 5, that in the short term, battery energy storage systems (BESS) would help ease the operation of power plants and prevent more unwanted outages.
“We don’t actually need more base load plants…The long-term solution is to have a decentralized, distributed and flexible grid,” Dalusung said.

For this to happen, the energy expert explained, more BESSes have to be deployed in areas where they can immediately discharge stored energy when peak demand spikes, and develop local embedded power generation systems to provide energy close to where it is needed. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Tributes pour in for labor leader Dolores Huerta: ‘Fought for farm workers to the very end’
articles.summary:
Lawmakers, activists and union leaders across the US remember the co-founder of United Farm Workers union

Following the news that Dolores Huerta – the civil rights icon who popularized the…

blocks.text: Following the news that Dolores Huerta – the civil rights icon who popularized the rallying cry “Sí, se puede! – had died at the age of 96 on Wednesday, activists, lawmakers and civil rights leaders paid tribute to Hureta’s long and lasting legacy.

In California – where Huerta helped found the United Farm Workers (UFW) union – her death was deeply felt. It was in California’s central valley that she laid the foundations for the United Farm Workers, and helped organize the 1965 Delano grape strike – a national boycott of table grapes that resulted in better wages and working conditions for grape pickers. Several schools in California bear her name, and murals across the state depict her likeness. And in 2018, California declared 10 April – her birthday – Dolores Huerta Day.

“From the fields of California to the halls of Congress and the White House, Dolores dedicated her life to ensuring that every voice – especially those too often silenced – was heard,” said Hector Sanchez Barba, the president of the voter mobilization organization Mi Familia Vota. “Her historic rallying cry, ‘Sí, se puede,’ is not just a slogan; it is a living call to action that continues to unite and inspire millions across the world.”

“Our greatest monument to her memory is for the union she helped found to continue to grow. Dolores fought for farm workers to the very end of her life,” said UFW president Teresa Romero. “The greatest possible tribute to her life is for her work of organizing to continue.”

Huerta’s legacy is national and international; her portrait hangs at some US embassies and schools in several US states are named after her. She helped negotiate national immigration policy, and remained, until her death, intimately involved in promoting civil and labor rights in Washington DC and across the US.
Tributes also came from some of California’s biggest political names, including Nancy Pelosi, the former House speaker, Gavin Newsom, the governor, and former vice-president Kamala Harris.

“Dolores was a dear friend, and we all responded to her rallying cry, ‘Sí se puede,’ which inspired generations of Americans to believe in the power of collective action,” said Pelosi. “May it be a comfort to her family and loved ones that so many mourn their loss and are praying for them at this sad time.”

“I was blessed to know Dolores for many years and proud to organize alongside my dear friend to champion working families and immigrant rights,” said Harris. “I will always be grateful for her support and friendship. We will honor her legacy by continuing the fight for the dignity of every person.”

“Dolores Huerta represented the best of us,” said Newsom. “California – and the United States – would not be what we are today without her resolute spirit, her passion for justice and fairness, and her commitment to those overlooked and forgotten.”

“The best tribute we can pay is to carry on the work, which means standing with workers, defending civil rights and organizing for a more just California,” echoed Alex Padilla, US senator representing California.

“¡Adiós, Dolores! You were everywhere. You did everything,” said Xavier Becerra, the former California attorney general and former US health secretary who is running for governor. “If you want to know where a leader will take you, know where they come from. Dolores never let us forget where she came from. Si, se pudo [Yes, we did].”

Lawmakers across the US, including Alexandria Ocasio Cortez, the New York congressperson, also hailed her trailblazing legacy. “For decades after the Delano Grape Strike, she continued to organize for the rights of working people, women and immigrants. She continued to fight for the idea that when ordinary people come together, they can change the course of history,” said Ocasio Cortez. “While we mourn her devastating loss, we will continue her fight to build a country where every worker, regardless of race, gender, or economic status, is treated with dignity.”
Lawmakers thanked Huerta for her efforts to promote female candidates to public office.

Eloise Gómez Reyes, the state senator who brought legislation in 2018 to mark 10 April as Dolores Huerta Day in California, said that she was mourning “the loss of someone who profoundly shaped my own life”.

“Dolores Huerta taught generations of us that we did not have to accept the world as it was. That ordinary people, working together, could challenge powerful institutions, overcome injustice, and build something better. She didn’t simply open doors for women like me. She taught us that we had the power to open them for others,” Reyes said.

Hilda Solis, a former Democratic congresswoman who became the first Latina to serve in a cabinet position as Barack Obama’s labor secretary, thanked Huerta for her mentorship. “Growing up in the San Gabriel Valley, I rarely saw Latinas in positions of leadership. Dolores was one of the few women who showed me what was possible,” she said. “From the state legislature to Congress and my time serving in President Barack Obama’s cabinet, Dolores remained a constant in my life. We joined demonstrations and rallies, stood with workers fighting for their rights and demanded action when people in power looked away … Dolores understood the importance of showing up, bearing witness and refusing to let the suffering of women go ignored.”

Huerta for years was considered the second-in-command to UFW co-founder César Chávez – and spoke about how she had to fight the sexism within the movement, and was often forced to cede credit to Chávez. Earlier this year, in the aftermath of a New York Times investigation uncovering Chávez’ pattern of sexual abuse of women and girls, Huerta revealed that Chávez had raped her, too.
“I believed that exposing the truth would hurt the farmworker movement I have spent my entire life fighting for,” she said, explaining why she had stayed silent about her abuse for so long.

But after sharing her story, she learned that her fear would not bear out. Across the US, officials looked to renaming streets that once bore Chávez’s name with Huerta’s. Murals centering Chávez were replaced with Huerta’s image, or images depicting the larger farmworker movement.

“Her guidance transcended generations, nationalities, and borders. She touched so many people as she fought for justice, peace and equality. She never backed down,” said actor Rosario Dawson, who portrayed Huerta in a 2014 biopic of César Chávez. Dawson, who cofounded the organization Voto Latino, had worked with Huerta to rally voter turnout, and at times had openly disagreed with her politics, said that the civil rights leader had been a “mentor and a beacon of light”.
“¡Sí, se puede, Dolores! May we carry your light and joy as we forge the path for new generations,” she added.

Earlier this month, Microsoft also announced a new Surface Ultra laptop that runs on Nvidia’s artificial intelligence chips and will cost more than $2,500. Apple announced a similar touchscreen Macbook this week.

articles.title: Non-profit group leaks data of more than 40,000 homeland security workers
articles.summary:
Information released by Distributed Denial of Secrets is the third such government data disclosure in the last month

The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on Wednesday it has…

blocks.text: The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on Wednesday it has released data on more than 40,000 Department ⁠of Homeland Security (DHS) employees, including details about officials working in sensitive fields such as surveillance and human intelligence.
DHS did not immediately return a message seeking comment.

The disclosure – which the ⁠non-profit data transparency group says draws ⁠on information obtained ​by an entity calling itself “Department of Peace” – is the third government data leak to have made headlines in the past month.

In September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed ⁠the theft of a massive trove of data from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, including sensitive job details and medical information from thousands of bureau employees. Last week, the defense department was hit with ⁠a class action lawsuit following a breach that exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel.

The DHS data includes ​names, phone numbers and email addresses of employees from Immigration ‌and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border ‌Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and other DHS component agencies.

Also included in the data were job ‌titles and email groups, which, among other details, showed which agents were assigned to special operations, surveillance jobs, computer forensics and undercover work.

In a statement, Emma Best, a Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder, said the hacktivist known as “maia arson crimew” developed a search tool for the data that would allow the public to browse it. Best said the tool would “replace anonymity with accountability” and empower journalists, guide public records requests and boost congressional oversight.

The Department of Peace did not immediately respond ‌to a request for comment, but in a statement included with the data, it said that DHS employees “have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs” and that it hoped the data “can ​be used to limit further harm by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction”.
The Department of Peace in March claimed responsibility for hacking DHS and posting documents related to contracts with outside vendors.

Best’s statement said Department of Peace harvested the data from the Okta sign-on service used by DHS. Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. Okta said in response to a Reuters query: “Okta is ⁠secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised.”

Reuters could not immediately ​verify the authenticity of the entire data ​trove but it was able to match ​personal information of about six DHS employees named in the leak to credit bureau records and breach data ​carried by the dark ‌web intelligence platform District 4 ​Labs. In other cases, ​Reuters called three DHS employees directly and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach.

In several cases, the data tracked information available on DHS employees’ LinkedIn profiles. But in others, the data revealed nonpublic data about internal DHS organization charts or previously undisclosed programs or operations.

articles.title: Embattled Bari Weiss says she is not ‘focused’ on declining 60 Minutes ratings
articles.summary:
CBS News editor-in-chief sidesteps viewership concerns and says flagship show doing ‘tremendously well’

CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss has spoken publicly for the first time about the…

blocks.text: CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss has spoken publicly for the first time about the ratings challenges the network has experienced under her year-long tenure, sidestepping concerns about diminished viewership at the Sunday show 60 Minutes by saying it was not her top priority.

“I could never build anything if I were focused on the precise number of people that happen to tune in to the second feature on 60 Minutes on a given Sunday,” she said at an industry conference on Wednesday organized by the tech publication the Information. The news organization did not offer press credentials.
Overall, Weiss said the show was doing “tremendously well”.

Weiss completely overhauled 60 Minutes in late May, ousting the show’s executive producer and parting ways with three top correspondents, including Scott Pelley. But the show has struggled to even match last season’s viewership, which averaged 9.1 million viewers per episode.

The show’s most recent episode drew just 5.64 million viewers, “one of the smallest audiences for the program in years”, Variety reported. The show was the lowest-rated sixth episode of the weekly show this century, a feat also achieved by the fourth episode of the show.

The show’s ratings are heavily dependent on whether it is preceded by a highly watched NFL football game. Ratings for the show have been low despite a strong run of guest bookings and news-making segments. Viewership hasn’t been all bad, either – the 4 October edition of the show drew an average of more than 10 million total viewers.

Weiss was also asked about parent company Skydance’s recent merger with Warner Bros Discovery, the parent company of CNN. While Weiss was initially rumored to potentially lead the cable news network, chief executive David Ellison instead opted to keep CNN chief executive Mark Thompson in place – for the time being, at least.
Asked whether she might be interested in running CNN, Weiss replied: “I want to focus on doing CBS News, trust me. This is a big enough challenge.”

Weiss said she is not focused on criticism of her tenure at CBS News, which has come from inside and outside the building. Her strategy has been to “put the blinders on, tune out the noise and focus”, adding: “I’m not doing anything I’m doing for popularity’s sake.”

articles.title: Girl seriously injured in wolf attack at German wildlife park
articles.summary: The eight-year-old was in an enclosure with other children and a staff member when she was attacked.

blocks.text: An eight-year-old girl has been seriously injured in a wolf attack at a German wildlife park.
She was inside an enclosure at the Johannismühle park in Brandenburg, south of Berlin, with a staff member and two other children when the attack happened, police said.
They said in a statement that the "precise circumstances of the incident are the subject of an ongoing police investigation".
The girl was taken to hospital by helicopter after the incident on Wednesday. No one else was injured.
The park, in the town of Baruth/Mark, has been closed temporarily and is set to reopen on 2 November, according to its website, which did not give further details.
The park keeps grey and arctic wolves, along with other animals including the brown bear and lynx.
The girl was injured by at least one animal and suffered head injuries, according to German newspaper Bild.
It reported that the incident happened before the park opened at 10:00 local time (09:00 GMT) and that the girl could have been taking part in a special visit.
Johannismühle offers small group tours to allow visitors to spend time with some animals, with its site mentioning feeding wolves or petting a llama.
The incident comes after a number of other animal attacks at zoos and wildlife parks in Europe.
A keeper at a Dutch zoo died this week after being mauled by a leopard, and a man was killed by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park earlier this month.

articles.title: Australian SAS officers knew about unlawful ‘throwdowns’ on dead Afghans, report says
articles.summary:
Nothing done to stop planting weapons on dead Afghans, ADF inspector says, as ‘breakdown of command’ allowed ‘egregious behaviour’

  • Get our

blocks.text: Some Australian SAS officers knew that soldiers under their command were using “throwdowns” – planting weapons on dead Afghan civilians to portray them as combatants – but did nothing to stop the unlawful practice, a previously unpublished military report has said.

Posted online this week, the executive summary of a 2021 investigation into the “cultural context” of the special operations command by the inspector general of the Australian Defence Force (IGADF) is scathing about the “breakdown of command” and the erosion of military discipline during special forces operations in Afghanistan, which “resulted in episodes of potential and actual egregious behaviour”.

A previously published IGADF report, the Brereton Inquiry, made public in 2020, found credible information that Australian special forces personnel murdered 39 Afghan civilians and prisoners. But the Brereton report largely exonerated officers, saying the “criminal behaviour” it uncovered “was conceived, committed, continued, and concealed at patrol commander level”. Patrol commanders in the Australian SAS are not commissioned officers, they are typically corporals or sergeants.

However, the newly released report, commissioned after the Brereton findings by former defence force chief – and SAS officer – Angus Campbell in 2021, found some SAS officers knew about alleged “unlawful behaviour” and did not act to stop them.

“Officers with actual knowledge of misconduct in-theatre, including notably the use of throwdowns to effect in fraudulent reporting, or rumours of misconduct, did not take effective action to investigate and address these issues.”
The unlawful behaviour identified by the IGADF revealed “a breakdown of command” and ineffective leadership.

“The proper functioning of the ADF as a hierarchical system relies upon the enforcement of rules at all levels. A failure to do so has a corrosive effect on behaviours, morale and ultimately, military discipline, which in this case resulted in episodes of potential and actual egregious behaviour.”

SAS officers allowed the regiment to develop an “uncontrolled ‘warrior’ ethos” and the long, grinding, nature of the Afghan conflict, to which a small cohort of SAS soldiers were repeatedly sent on dangerous, corrosive deployments, contributed to moral injury and impaired decision-making.
“The group dynamic within a special forces deployment influences the shift in moral compass of some individuals,” the report said.
“The incremental shift in moral compass in response to violence, killing, morally questionable decisions and unconventional features, can create moral injury.”

The report found that the excessively secretive and insular nature of the SAS also contributed to worsening standards as did an “inversion” of the chain of command, where senior non-commissioned officers were able to dominate officers who were, ostensibly, their superiors.
“This resulted in junior officers being effectively subservient to non-commissioned officers, and occupying a position which can best be described as ‘learned helplessness’.”

The report cited the fact SAS soldiers were consistently allowed to drink alcohol while on deployment in Afghanistan – in defiance of orders imposed on others – “sent the strong signal to those involved that the rules did not apply to them”.
The use of “throwdowns” was a known breach that officers failed to stop.

“The unwillingness to challenge non-commissioned officers was particularly apparent from the breakdown of military discipline through a lack of proper supervision. The failure to address the widely known use of throwdowns is an example of this.
“This was also a manifestation of a broader breakdown of military discipline within the SAS regiment. The tolerance of officers of overt non-compliance sent a powerful signal.”

Similarly, soldiers wrote false reports of their actions on the battlefield, focused on rules of engagement and laced with circumlocution, which “assisted perpetrators of misconduct to conceal their actions”.

“A particular manifestation was the use of variations of a standard phrase ‘manoeuvring to a position of tactical advantage’, to describe the actions of civilian ‘squirters’ as direct participants in hostilities, which justified engagement … under the rules of engagement. The expression was used with such regularity that it lost meaning.”

The report’s executive summary says there was “a significant failure of good leadership and effective command” across the SAS commanders, and that the reporting systems designed to prevent misconduct had become “depleted and largely unreliable”, giving officers “a false level of assurance”.
“The culture of the Special Operations Task Group … was not the cause of misconduct but created an environment which enabled misconduct by a few to occur.”
Defence had previously refused to release the report despite it being the subject of freedom of information requests and an attempt to force its disclosure in the Senate.

articles.title: New book makes fiery claims about Jared Kushner’s finances in Trump’s first term
articles.summary:
Kushner threatens to sue, denying allegations that two slush funds were set up to influence his Middle East role

A new book containing incendiary claims about

blocks.text: A new book containing incendiary claims about Jared Kushner’s financial dealings during Donald Trump’s first term has ignited a political and media firestorm.

The book by author Matthew Cole is called Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East and was released in the US this week. An excerpt was published by Vanity Fair last Thursday, and immediately drew a furious response from Kushner, who called its claims “completely insane”. The book contains numerous allegations about Kushner, whose father-in-law is Trump and who has served as one of his top diplomatic envoys in the Middle East – the most explosive of which are claims linking him to huge bank accounts allegedly funded by Gulf states.

Kusher denounced the book on his site last week, and writing on X: “We denied every one of these claims on the record, yet the author failed to provide a single shred of evidence to substantiate any of them.” He has demanded that Vanity Fair retract the excerpt and has threatened legal action against the book’s publisher, Simon & Schuster.

He added: “During the period in question, I was one of the most scrutinized people in the world, subjected to intense media coverage, multiple congressional investigations, and a special counsel investigation. I voluntarily cooperated with these investigations, providing over 30 hours of testimony. None of these allegations ever surfaced, because none of these events ever happened.”
The Guardian contacted Kushner’s legal counsel from Clare Locke as well as Chad Mizelle for comment and received no response.

Cole’s sources are predominantly anonymous and he does not print images of emails or other documentation to support his reporting. Extensive footnotes indicate sources of information, including confidential interviews.

In the book, the top intelligence official in the United Arab Emirates, Ali Al Shamsi, is reported to have called Kushner “the most expensive employee we’ve ever had”. The book details alleged payments into two “slush fund” bank accounts allegedly set up for Kushner by Emirati prince Mohamed bin Zayed (MBZ) and Saudi Arabian prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) during Trump’s first term. The Guardian contacted the Saudi Arabian and Emirati embassies for comment and did not receive a response.
In the book, Cole claims the accounts were partially managed by Kushner on an iPhone hacked by Russian and Dutch intelligence.

But despite the Emirati spymaster’s opinion of Kushner, Cole alleges that the New Jersey real estate scion was not entirely trusted. Cole describes a dangerous world in which blackmail is as common a tool of statecraft as torture and murder, as in the cases of the Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi, killed on the orders of MBS in Turkey in 2018, and the Emirati journalist and poet Habib Al Sayegh, whose killing by agents of MBZ in 2019 is described by Cole.

Kushner continues to steer US foreign policy despite having no official role, with questions about his business interests accompanying him as he travels the world with New York real estate magnate Steve Witkoff, this week seeking peace in Ukraine, if on terms favorable to Russia.

In response, an attorney “who has represented President Trump in multiple defamation lawsuits”, Alejandro Brito, told Cole that, “during his time working for President Trump, Kushner ‘always represented and sought the interests of the United States and the President of the United States and did not make any agreements or arrangements with leaders or officials in foreign countries that were not agreed by the President of the United States and in the best interests of the United States.’” He further said that “[a]ny allegation that Kushner knew of, had access to, had authorization for or engaged in or directed any conduct related to any government-funded or government-linked bank account is totally false and defamatory”.
Brito told Cole that “‘there are no accounts and never were.’” Cole writes that the Dutch government refused to comment in response to his questions about the alleged hacking of Kushner’s phone.

According to Cole, MBZ and MBS wanted Kushner to help achieve their “vision of a new Middle East, one in which Israel would become an integral part of the region, recognized diplomatically by Gulf Arabs today and eventually by the rest of the Arab world; the Palestinians would end their conflict with Israel and accept a peace built on prosperity; Islamic extremism would be defeated; and Iran’s expansionism and militancy would retreat, either by persuasion or force.”

Nearly 10 years later, the US and Israel are planning new strikes in their eight-month war with Iran; Saudi Arabia is at war with Houthi rebels in Yemen, and Israel has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians in Gaza since the Hamas attacks of 7 October 2023.

Kushner entered Trump’s first administration with his wife, Ivanka Trump, as close presidential advisers. MBZ and MBS, Cole claims, saw a chance to secure the best access money could buy. Cole alleges that in early 2017 the two princes “proposed to give Kushner a fund, a bank account, which the two leaders, working with Jared, would use to identify and pay for projects and foreign policy goals to advance for President Trump’s benefit”.

According to Cole, an idea to fund Trump’s proposed wall on the US border with Mexico apparently did not work out but the author claims that “MBZ and MBS initially, and then MBZ alone, put at least $2bn into at least two banks for Kushner.” Classifying the accounts as “Alpha” and “Beta”, Cole claims the Alpha account was held at First Abu Dhabi Bank, the largest in UAE, and contained “roughly $750m” to be “used as a foreign policy fund” overseen by Kushner and MBZ and meant to help end the Israel-Palestine conflict.

Cole quotes a source who says he knew of the UAE’s alleged deal with Kushner as saying: “‘Jared was looking for shortcuts in his diplomacy.’” Cole writes: “This person held discussions with both senior UAE and Israeli officials about the secret financial arrangement between Kushner, the UAE, and, at least initially, Saudi Arabia. ‘Jared promised MBZ that he’d push their agenda with Trump if they participated in a fund. He wanted normalization with Israel so that business could take off,’” the source alleged.

The same source claimed that “a slush fund – a shared pool of money for off-the-books diplomatic objectives – was a common form of Gulf Arab government corruption … ‘The Emiratis and the Saudis do this once a year. A billion or two is nothing for them, and if it gets them what they want, it’s money well spent.’”

Citing “a person briefed on the Beta account”, Cole claims it contained “roughly $1bn” and at the suggestion of the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, was moved by MBZ to the Israeli Central Bank via Azerbaijan, a favored conduit for laundering money.

“It is … unclear how Kushner used the money the UAE deposited into the Beta account for him,” Cole alleges, “but according to the person with knowledge of the money, its allocation was for Kushner’s personal benefit.”

Kushner’s attorney, Brito, told Cole his client “had no financial relationships with any foreign countries or leaders”, adding that his “complete financial disclosures are publicly available in his OGE [office of government ethics] form 278e filings during this period.”

Cole alleges that the “Alpha” account established for Kushner in Trump’s first term was drained by failed schemes and Kushner’s access was cut off. “It is unclear if the Israeli government allowed Kushner access to the Beta bank account” after the end of Trump’s first term, Cole writes.

Cole also examines the widely reported story about how Kushner ultimately secured Qatari investment in 666 Fifth Avenue, a marquee Manhattan property, thereby profiting from interests on both sides of a bitterly divided Middle East, given Saudi Arabia and UAE’s rivalry with Qatar. (Kushner has denied engaging in any conflicts of interest.)

In Trump’s second term, Kushner’s diplomatic work has been dogged by questions about another massive financial asset: a $2bn investment by the Saudi sovereign wealth fund in Kushner’s Affinity Partners private equity firm, made after Trump left power in 2021. Cole quotes an unnamed Arab official and Affinity investor who claimed: “We don’t pay Jared because he’s a savvy investor. We pay him to keep him happy. That keeps his father-in-law happy.”

Cole writes: “Deep relationships with MBZ, MBS, Emir Al Thani [of Qatar], and Bibi Netanyahu were useful as [Kushner] shuttled between capitals, trying to find a way to end the daily slaughter in Gaza. But as it had been when he was a government employee, there was little record of what his investors were negotiating with him.”

In his epilogue, Cole writes that Kushner “declined multiple requests for an on-the-record interview for the book”, adding that he “first contacted him with a list of questions in May 2026 and followed up via email twice more, asking additional questions.”

Through his lawyers, Kushner denounced all of Cole’s reporting. Also on X, Chad Mizelle, a Trump administration lawyer who identified himself as “Jared’s attorney”, said: “The central allegation in this book is categorically false. These are not questions of interpretation or competing recollections: there are no bank accounts. They don’t exist. These are egregious and defamatory claims without a shred of evidence to substantiate them.”
